rationale: Lycopolitan numeral 'twenty' (= Sahidic ϫⲟⲩⲱⲧ); structures the discourse about the twenty characters/members of humanity in this kephalaion.
Lycopolitan/orthographic variant of ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'days' with ⲑ for ⲍ; appears in the construction [ⲛⲍ̄]ⲑⲟⲩⲉ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ 'seven holy days.'
Greek loanword πεντηκοστή 'fiftieth' = the Christian Pentecost season (50 days from Easter), here Manichaean-typologically identified with ⲡⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲅ̄ ⲛ̄ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'the Fifty of the great days.'

proposed_english: the Fifty of the great days
rationale: Manichaean technical term for the Pentecost-period reinterpreted as a cosmic feast of fifty holy days during which the Living Food (= Call and Answer) sufficed for the disciples and made them rich.
ⲣ̄- + ϣⲉ ('hundred') = 'become a hundred.' Describes the expansion of the holy fifty days into a hundred — likely a Manichaean liturgical extension or typological doubling of the Pentecost period.

Obscure overlined form recurring in this kephalaion in the construction ⲡⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ ⲁ̄ⲃ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ. Functionally serves to link Call and Answer as joint subject of the conveying action. Etymology unclear: possibly abbreviated verb (ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth'?), dual marker, or Aramaic-derived element. Flagged for parallel research.
